nodes.content: Design a multi-region secret broker reconciling emergency credential revocation, partition availability, and rollback-safe rotation.
requirements: Revoked credentials become unusable within 60 seconds, including during network partitions and broker replica rollback.
Unrevoked workloads maintain 99.9% authentication success during 30-second regional partitions overlapping credential rotation.

nodes.content: Use 55-second quorum-signed leases, refresh every 15 seconds, overlap rotation keys, and enforce HSM epochs; partitioned brokers cannot renew.
What lease TTL, refresh cadence, and rollback guard allow partitioned authentication without extending revoked-credential validity?
HSM epochs and 55-second leases refreshed every 15 seconds, with ≤5-second skew, yield ≥99.9% 30-second-partition availability and ≤60-second revocation.
Simulate worst-timed revocation, 30-second partitioned rotation, and broker rollback; measure revocation latency and workload authentication success.
Run PartitionRotate-60 simulation over 1 million logins, sweeping revocation phase, rotating keys, 30-second partitions, ±5-second skew, and snapshot rollback.
PartitionRotate-60 recorded 65-second revocation latency with opposing ±5-second clocks; unrevoked authentication success was 99.95%.
Replacing 55-second leases and 15-second refreshes with 50-second leases and 5-second refreshes should achieve ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% availability.
Rerun PartitionRotate-60 with 50-second leases and 5-second refreshes; sweep revocation timing, ±5-second skew, 30-second partitioned rotation, and rollback.
PartitionRotate-60 recorded 60-second maximum revocation latency and 99.94% unrevoked authentication success across ±5-second skew, 30-second partitions, and rollback.
Adopt 50-second leases with 5-second refreshes and HSM epochs; 55-second leases breached revocation, while revised simulation met both targets.
Simulate adopted leases under correlated refresh failures, 30-second partitioned rotation, and rollback; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
PartitionRotate-60 resilience report records correlated refresh failures, rollback traces, revocation latency, and authentication success during partitioned rotation.
Can correlated refresh failures and broker rollback during partitioned rotation breach 60-second revocation or 99.9% authentication targets?
Issue 45-second workload-bound tokens, refresh every 5 seconds, and pre-stage dual rotation keys behind monotonic HSM revocation counters.
Prototype workload-bound 45-second tokens and pre-staged rotation keys; chaos-test partitions and rollback for revocation latency and authentication success.
Replay resilience-report traces with 45-second tokens, 5-second refresh, dual keys, and HSM counters; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
TokenReplay-45 report contains per-trace revocation latency and unrevoked authentication success for 45-second tokens versus adopted 50-second leases.
Compare TokenReplay-45 and PartitionRotate-60 resilience reports across correlated failures and rollback, checking ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication success.
TokenReplay-45 recorded 55-second maximum revocation latency and 99.96% authentication success during correlated refresh failures, partitioned rotation, and rollback.
Adopt 45-second workload-bound tokens: 55-second revocation versus 60 seconds, and 99.96% authentication success versus 99.94% for leases.
Run broker-chaos trials comparing both designs under rollback, 30-second partitioned rotation, and ±5-second skew; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
Live rollback erased p2’s staged key, yielding 99.72% authentication success versus p1’s 99.93%; both revoked within 60 seconds.
Can workload-bound tokens and HSM-fenced dual keys preserve revocation safety and authentication availability during partitioned rotation and rollback?
Persisting dual rotation keys in rollback-resistant HSM storage should restore ≥99.9% authentication while retaining ≤60-second revocation during partitions.
Replay staged-key rollback failures with HSM-persisted dual keys during 30-second partitions; measure authentication success and worst-case revocation latency.
With HSM-persisted dual keys, rollback trials reached 99.95% authentication success, up from 99.72%, while maximum revocation latency stayed 55 seconds.
Use 20-second regionally signed tokens with 30-second partition fencing and HSM-persisted overlapping keys to bound stale issuance.
Can regionally signed tokens maintain ≥99.9% authentication through 30-second partitions without extending revocation latency beyond 60 seconds?
Replay PartitionRotate-60 resilience traces using 20-second regional tokens, 30-second fencing, and HSM keys; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
PartitionRotate-60 replay measured 55-second maximum revocation latency and 99.92% unrevoked authentication success during 30-second partitions and rollback.
In live 30-second partitions with ≤5-second clock skew, regional tokens should keep revocation ≤55 seconds and authentication ≥99.9%.
Live-test regional and workload-bound tokens with HSM-persisted keys during 30-second partitioned rotation and rollback; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
Live trials: regional tokens achieved 99.94% authentication and 54-second revocation; workload-bound tokens fell to 99.84% despite HSM keys.
Adopt regional tokens with HSM-persisted overlapping keys: live trials met both targets, and rollback trials validated key persistence.
Implement regional tokens and HSM-backed dual keys; canary 30-second partitioned rotation and rollback, gating on ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication.
Implement HSM-backed key overlap and 20-second regional token issuance; canary partitioned rotation and snapshot rollback while tracking both SLOs.
Broker v0.3 implements 20-second regional tokens, HSM-backed key overlap, partition fencing, and revocation and authentication canary dashboards.
PartitionRotate-60 replay found zero stale-epoch tokens issued across 10,000 broker rollbacks with HSM-persisted rotation keys.
Pre-issue workload-bound 30-second renewal vouchers, enforce HSM monotonic epochs, and halt voucher use 25 seconds after quorum loss.
HSM-fenced 30-second vouchers with 25-second quorum-loss cutoff should sustain ≥99.9% authentication and ≤60-second revocation despite correlated failures and rollback.
Extend Broker v0.3 with 25-second-fenced vouchers; inject correlated failures, 30-second partitioned rotation, and rollback; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
Voucher canary reached 99.97% authentication, but worst-case revocation took 64 seconds when quorum vanished immediately before voucher issuance.
Instrument Broker v0.3’s 25-second voucher canary under ±5-second skew and n43’s pre-issuance quorum loss; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
HSM-timestamped cutoff removed a 9-second detection lag; repeat pre-issuance-loss trials at ±5-second skew measured 59-second revocation and 99.94% authentication.
Can HSM-fenced vouchers survive worst-timed quorum loss and rollback without exceeding 60-second revocation or dropping below 99.9% authentication?
HSM-timestamped 25-second voucher fencing should keep revocation ≤60 seconds and authentication ≥99.9% under worst-timed quorum loss and rollback.
Replay n43’s worst-timed loss with n45’s HSM cutoff across rollback and 30-second partitions; measure peak revocation latency and authentication success.
HSM-cutoff replay across 10,000 worst-timed loss and rollback trials peaked at 59-second revocation with 99.94% unrevoked authentication success.
Retain regional tokens: initial vouchers breached 60 seconds; HSM-corrected vouchers reach 59 seconds without improving 99.94% authentication.
Shadow-test retained regional tokens against HSM-fenced vouchers under worst-timed quorum loss and rollback; gate ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication.
Run Broker v0.3 shadow canary comparing regional tokens and HSM-fenced vouchers during 30-second partitioned rotation, quorum loss, and replica rollback.
ShadowCanary-30 report compares regional-token and voucher revocation latency and authentication success across quorum loss, partitioned rotation, and rollback.
Grant regional issuers 35-second HSM-fenced signing capabilities, issue 20-second mTLS certificates, and HSM-stage overlapping trust roots.
Prototype HSM-fenced regional signing and staged roots; chaos-test 30-second partitions, rotation, and rollback for revocation latency and authentication success.
Replay ShadowCanary-30 and TokenReplay-45 traces using 35-second HSM signing capabilities and 20-second certificates; compare revocation and authentication metrics.
Trace replay measured 55-second maximum revocation latency and 99.97% authentication success with HSM signing capabilities, versus 99.94% for regional tokens.
Do HSM-fenced regional signing capabilities preserve ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication when trust-root rotation overlaps a partition?
HSM-staged overlapping roots should maintain ≥99.9% authentication and ≤60-second revocation during 30-second partitioned root rotation and rollback.
Using replay-validated signing capabilities, live-test staged-root rotation during 30-second partitions and rollback; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
Live partitioned root-rotation trials recorded 57-second maximum revocation latency and 99.93% authentication success despite replica rollback.
Retain regional tokens: signing capabilities fell from 99.97% replay to 99.93% live, below regional tokens’ 99.94%.
Roll out regional tokens with HSM-persisted overlapping keys; test 30-second partitioned rotation and rollback, gating ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication.
Using ShadowCanary-30 and TokenReplay-45 baselines, canary regional-token rollout during partitioned rotation and rollback; verify ≤60-second revocation and ≥99.9% authentication.
RegionalToken-Rollout canary report records partitioned-rotation and rollback revocation latency, authentication success, and SLO gate outcomes against both baselines.
